title: Package GPIO Control Panel as Linux-runnable app bundle

requirements.summary: Configure Vite build to use relative base path for Linux deployment
acceptanceCriteria: Running `npm run build` produces a `dist/` folder where all JS, CSS, and asset URLs are relative (start with `./`).
The built `index.html` loads correctly when opened from a local Apache server at any virtual host path.
No absolute `/assets/` paths appear in the compiled output.

file_operations.description: Update the Vite configuration to set `base: './'` (relative base path) in the build configuration so that all compiled asset references use relative URLs. This ensures the built static bundle works when served from any directory on a local Linux Apache server or file system without requiring absolute path configuration.

requirements.summary: Update GPIO HTTP endpoint to use plain HTTP localhost
acceptanceCriteria: HTTP POST requests to the GPIO server use `http://localhost:3000` as the base URL.
No mixed-content or HTTPS errors appear in the browser console when sending GPIO signals from a locally served page.
The DebugHttpPanel successfully fires test requests to `http://localhost:3000` when a GPIO server is running.

file_operations.description: Change the GPIO server base URL from HTTPS to plain HTTP (`http://localhost:3000`) to prevent mixed-content errors when the frontend is served from a local Apache server on Linux. Ensure the sendGpioSignal function uses this HTTP endpoint for all POST requests.

requirements.summary: Update Linux bundle packaging scripts to include all deployment artifacts
acceptanceCriteria: Running `./scripts/package_linux_bundle.sh` produces a `.tar.gz` file containing the frontend `dist/`, backend canister artifacts, and all helper scripts.
The bundle includes a top-level `README.md` or `INSTALL.md` with step-by-step Linux setup instructions.
Extracting and following the included instructions on a Linux machine with `dfx` and Apache results in a working control panel accessible via browser.

file_operations.description: Update the packaging script to include all necessary deployment artifacts in the timestamped .tar.gz bundle: built frontend `dist/` folder, backend canister WASM and declarations, `dfx.json`, Apache vhost configuration example, the `rpi_event_runner.sh` script, and a top-level `INSTALL.md` or `README.md` with comprehensive Linux setup instructions. Ensure the bundle structure allows easy extraction and deployment on a fresh Linux machine.

Update the launcher script to ensure it correctly starts a local ICP replica, deploys the control panel backend, and supports stop/clean/help subcommands. Verify the script paths reference the bundled artifacts correctly and include error handling for missing prerequisites (dfx, npm, Apache).

Create a comprehensive installation guide for the Linux bundle that includes: prerequisites checklist (Node.js, dfx, Apache), step-by-step extraction instructions, dfx replica deployment steps, Apache vhost configuration and serving of the `dist/` folder, GPIO server setup on port 3000, verification steps, and a troubleshooting section covering common issues (CORS, mixed content, port conflicts, permission errors).

requirements.summary: Create comprehensive Linux installation guide documentation
acceptanceCriteria: The document lists all prerequisites with recommended versions.
Step-by-step instructions are present for Apache vhost setup, dfx replica startup, and frontend serving.
A troubleshooting section addresses common issues (CORS, mixed content, port conflicts).

file_operations.description: Expand the existing Linux bundle documentation to provide comprehensive coverage of: prerequisites (Node.js, dfx, Apache) with recommended versions; detailed step-by-step instructions for building the bundle, extracting it, deploying the local ICP replica, configuring Apache to serve the `dist/` folder, starting the GPIO server on port 3000; verification steps to confirm the full stack is operational; and an expanded troubleshooting section addressing CORS issues, mixed content warnings, port conflicts, Apache configuration errors, and dfx replica problems.
